title: Composition coherence of scalar inverse-image units and coefficients
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $A,B,C$ schemes, and $f_A:A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $f_B:B\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $f_C:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ structure maps. Let $a:A\to B$ and $b:B\to C$ satisfy $a\gg f_B=f_A$ and $b\gg f_C=f_B$, and let $F$ be an $\mathcal O_C$-module. Use the scalar sheaf, inverse-image functor, constant-unit isomorphisms, coefficient maps, scalar morphism functor and normalized tensor-pullback comparison of [def-sc-field-linear-module-cohomology-operations]. Write $L_t=\mathrm{scalarInverseImage}(t)$, $P_t=\mathrm{tensorPullback}(t)$, $u_t=\mathrm{scalarInverseUnitIso}(t)^{-1}$, $j_t=\mathrm{scalarPullbackCoefficient}(t)$ and $q_F=(\mathrm{scalarPullbackCompIso}(a,b))_F^{-1}$. Define $e:L_{a\gg b}\cong L_b\circ L_a$ by uniqueness of left adjoints between the inverse-image adjunction for $a\gg b$ and the composite inverse-image adjunction for $b$ then $a$; their right adjoints are definitionally equal sheaf pushforwards. Then $u_{a\gg b}\gg e_{\mathbf1_C}=u_a\gg L_a(u_b)$ and $e_{\mathrm{scalarSheaf}(f_C,F)}\gg L_a(j_{b,F})\gg j_{a,P_bF}\gg\mathrm{scalarHom}(f_A,q_F)=j_{a\gg b,F}$. These assertions require no flatness, quasi-coherence or nonempty-scheme hypothesis.

proof.text: Construct e by Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq. Its unit equation says that the composite inverse-image unit equals the successive units. The constant sheaf functor has the global-sections adjunction. Both constant-unit composites have the same adjoint: the section assigning each scalar its constant section. Apply naturality of the constant-sheaf comparison and the unit equation to obtain the first equality.

Apply the inverse-image adjunction hom equivalence to the second equality, and evaluate on every open U and section s of F. By exists_scalarPullbackCoefficient, the adjoints of the coefficient maps are the normalized tensor-pullback units. The comparison scalarPullbackCompIso is defined by left-adjoint uniqueness and thus carries the composite tensor unit to the successive units. The inverse-image comparison satisfies the corresponding unit equation. After postcomposition by q_F both adjoints consequently have identical components on s. Sheaf-morphism extensionality and injectivity of the hom equivalence give the equality. The argument uses equations of maps and does not cancel sections, so it also handles zero coefficients and empty schemes.

lean.statement:
theorem scalarInverseImageCompIso_coherence
    (k : Type w) [Field k] (A B C : Scheme.{w})
    (fA : A ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (fB : B ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    (fC : C ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (a : A ⟶ B) (b : B ⟶ C)
    (ha : a ≫ fB = fA) (hb : b ≫ fC = fB) (F : C.Modules) :
    (scalarInverseUnitIso (a ≫ b)).inv ≫
        (scalarInverseImageCompIso k a b).hom.app (𝟙_ (KSheaf C k)) =
      (scalarInverseUnitIso a).inv ≫
        (scalarInverseImage a).map (scalarInverseUnitIso b).inv ∧
    (scalarInverseImageCompIso k a b).hom.app (scalarSheaf fC F) ≫
        (scalarInverseImage a).map (scalarPullbackCoefficient fC fB b hb F) ≫
        scalarPullbackCoefficient fB fA a ha ((tensorPullback b).obj F) ≫
        scalarHom fA ((scalarPullbackCompIso a b).app F).inv =
      scalarPullbackCoefficient fC fA (a ≫ b)
        (by rw [Category.assoc, hb, ha]) F
